title: A product of two naturals each >= 1 is itself >= 1
statement: For natural numbers a and b, if 1 <= a and 1 <= b, then 1 <= a * b.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.one_le_mul : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat.le (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) x0) -> ((x3 : AxNat.le (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) x1) -> AxNat.le (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) (AxNat.mul x0 x1)))))

evidence.supports: Nat.one_le_mul is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- one_le_mul 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.one_le_mul[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted kernel gate, so a successful build IS the type-check; the command both performs it and prints the admitted type, which is copied verbatim into formal.statement.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat environment admits no trusted declaration
evidence.notes: Reports `nat: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0`, over the FULL trusted surface rather than Declaration::Axiom alone. The enumeration is per-environment, not per-theorem; it bounds this theorem's footprint because a proof cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain.

provenance.source: theorem name and canonical type read directly via nat_theorem_inventory, which prints render_lean of the admitted type.

notes: depends_on is literal, read off theorem_dependency_inventory's direct-edge output for this theorem (cross-checked against nat_theorem_inventory's own admitted type), keeping only edges whose target is itself a registered fact. Nat.mul_succ, also a direct dependency, has no fact row.
